# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — code-enforce write-tool arg correctness (normalize + auto-fill payment) + actionable errors
- Changes I made (real CODE, 4 tools; passing task 19 = cancel-only ⇒ zero blast radius):
  - book_reservation.py: normalize flights→{flight_number,date}, payment `id`→`payment_id`(drop `source`/`type`/extras), passengers→{first,last,dob}; auto-fill payment amount when backend says "total price is X" (single method→total; multi w/ exactly one credit_card→remainder). Targets wrong-arg book cluster (task 23; helps 8/25 if they reach book).
  - update_reservation_flights.py: normalize flights + dict payment_id; append actionable next-step to certificate / gift-card-balance errors; docstring stresses ENTIRE itinerary. (11,17,22,37)
  - update_reservation_baggages.py: enrich certificate / gift-card errors; normalize dict payment_id. (17,22)
  - update_reservation_passengers.py: normalize passengers; on count-mismatch fetch reservation and state EXACT required count. (17,22)
- Expected effect + safety: removes the two dominant book failures (payment-key pydantic crash + payment arithmetic) deterministically, and turns opaque update errors into recoverable ones. SAFE because the sole passing task (19) never calls book/update — verified by trace inspection — so these guards cannot change any passing trajectory. Each guard fires only on the violating condition (bad key / amount mismatch / error string); well-formed calls pass through unchanged (verified: correct single-payment call makes exactly one backend call).
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — iteration 1, LEDGER/JOURNAL empty (seed).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: pure ACTION-STALL / narrated-not-executed (8, 11, 25) and premature transfer_to_human_agents (12, 37). Tool surface cannot force a call or safely block escalation; would need a policy/prompt lever (not owned here) or a composite tool the model still must choose to call.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this is rejected, next lever: try making book_reservation's payment auto-fill also cover 2-gift-card/certificate splits, and consider a composite "search+book" tool to cut the round-trips that starve the stall tasks of turns.
- Focus next iteration: the ACTION-STALL cluster (largest, still open) and the update_reservation_flights refund/partial-itinerary cases.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.500 Δ=+0.389 · fixed={12, 37, 40} · broke={—} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
